title: Central Government's Obligation to Appoint Commissioners

content.scenario: The Central Government is setting up the Central Authority to exercise powers and discharge functions under the Consumer Protection Act. It appoints a Chief Commissioner and two other Commissioners as prescribed.
content.outcome: The Central Government's appointment of the Commissioners is valid as it is in accordance with the prescribed requirements, and the Central Authority can exercise its powers and discharge its functions under the Act.

user_queries: Who appoints the Commissioners of the Central Authority?
What is the role of the Central Authority?
How many Commissioners can be appointed?
